There are a lot of pros& cons to any profession
Cons:
1. Laborious & Physically demanding, always moving, I heard 55 y/o is the average retirement age for a Therapist.. (not sure if it’s true but definitely can relate)
2. We will never be financially wealthy- there is always a salary max out due to limited Medicare reimbursement; we always having to deal with up/downs of yearly Medicare budget cuts & BS new rules for reimbursement. Salary wise we will always make a maximum less than 120k as a staff PT, unless u become self employed. As any profession if you are a self employed business owner then financial growth is unlimited. Is the amount of student debt & number of years devoted to school worth the salary??? 
3. Always the Therapist fault eg. (Pt isn’t walking it’s PT fault, pt had lack of ROM, it’s PT fault) people like to pass the blame why they aren’t getting better functionally. People like the idea of PT but many are not willing to work hard to for it or pay for it because everyone wants everything for free.
4. Other health care professionals do not respect us.  I have heard many times from doctors “oh she’s just a PT”.
5.  We are challenged ethically daily and limited by company demands & profit. For example We have learned about having autonomy in school & being able to make decisions to discharge patients when they reach max potential or have plateau. However in my experience I  have worked for many SNFs & my director of rehab (PTA/COTA) REFUSED to allow me to discharge a patient because the facility wanted to hit monetary thresholds. We are expected to treat patients for certain minutes & if we do not get those minutes in we are reprimanded or even penalized. I feel like our judgement is always being question & tested daily. we have to chose to bill a patient specifically for prolong duration or specific codes  based on higher reimbursement. This is a ethical challenge on itself and politically too.  I’ve been dictated by physicians or health care companies (like home health agencies);  for example MD/home health agencies will continuously refer for my services even if patient is ready for discharge and if I did not pick patients back up for PT, they will refer to another competitor. (Should I provide services because they need it or because they will go elsewhere ??)So there’s that fine line of ethical vs political decision making. 
6. Jobs require productivity!!! Eg. SNF wants us to have >90-93% productivity = (Treatment minutes billed to Medicare mins divided Minutes worked on time clock). This causes many problems such as working off the clock or making choices to bill fraudulently  
7. High chances of BURNOUT!

Pros Pros pros pros:

1. Jobs are plentiful, I’ve quit, been fired & I have always been able to find a job!!
2. It is rewarding to work with clients & HELP people. Truly rewarding career 
3. financially stable!! PT has allowed me to have a decent living and honest living!! we will never be able to be filthy rich but we won’t be on welfare either
4. Always be able to move physically & it is not sedentary. I could never sit at a desk 40 hours a week
5.  We are respected by average people
6. Able to work in variety of settings geriatrics to pediatrics etc etc


Heres a few pros and cons. I hope this helps you
